overview: A backend-powered speaker discovery and content management platform for TorahAnytime. The system brings together lecture discovery, speaker profiles, featured content, and administrative publishing workflows using ClickHouse and MySQL.

development.docs: I worked on the backend architecture supporting speaker discovery and content management. ClickHouse powers lecture queries, while MySQL manages application content and administrative data. The implementation involved faceted filtering, SQL window functions, dictionaries, and query optimization to support efficient content retrieval. I also worked on speaker banners, featured content, ownership validation, and administrative controls.

interactions.docs: Users can discover lectures through speaker pages and filtering options. Administrators can manage featured content, speaker banners, and publishing settings. The backend connects these workflows while enforcing rules around which content can appear on different pages.

complexities.docs: One important challenge was balancing flexible content discovery with efficient database access. I addressed inefficient query patterns, including N+1 queries, through batching and query restructuring. Another challenge involved maintaining consistent ownership and visibility rules across different content placements.

security.docs: Administrative operations require appropriate access controls. I implemented validation to ensure content and banner assignments respect their intended ownership and placement rules, reducing the risk of content appearing in unintended locations.

overview: A high-performance data export and migration initiative supporting TorahAnytime's transition from RethinkDB to MySQL. A Go-based exporter processed approximately six million records in twelve minutes, compared with an earlier Node.js approach that processed roughly 300,000 records in sixteen hours.

development.docs: As part of the database migration effort, I developed a Go-based data exporter to handle large volumes of existing records. The work focused on improving throughput and reducing the time required to extract data from the legacy system. I also contributed to migrating application data and persistence logic from RethinkDB to MySQL.

interactions.docs: This was primarily a backend infrastructure project rather than a user-facing feature. Its purpose was to make large-scale data movement more practical and support the application's transition to its newer persistence architecture.

complexities.docs: The central challenge was the performance of the original export approach. An earlier Node.js implementation processed approximately 300,000 records over sixteen hours. The Go exporter processed approximately six million records in twelve minutes, substantially improving export throughput.

security.docs: The migration work operated on application data and required careful handling of database access and record integrity. The implementation focused on controlled data extraction and reliable transfer between persistence systems.

overview: A CSV import workflow for MyCelebrant that helps celebrants bring existing leads and ceremony records into the platform, with automatic field recognition, duplicate detection, flexible date parsing, and actionable validation feedback.

development.docs: I developed a bulk import workflow supporting leads and ceremonies. The implementation recognizes incoming CSV fields, handles different date formats, validates records, checks for duplicates, and creates valid application records through transactional database operations.

interactions.docs: The workflow reduces the manual effort required to move existing records into MyCelebrant. Users can provide their data in CSV format and receive row-level feedback about validation issues, making it easier to identify and correct problematic entries.

complexities.docs: Real-world CSV files are rarely consistent. Handling differences in column names, date representations, missing values, and duplicate records required a flexible parsing and validation approach. Transactional creation also helped maintain consistency when records depended on related database entities.

security.docs: The import process validates incoming data before creating records and operates within the application's existing access controls. Duplicate detection and transactional database operations help prevent inconsistent or unintended records.

overview: An embeddable lead capture system that allows celebrants to collect enquiries through forms on their own websites and automatically bring those enquiries into MyCelebrant's management workflows.

development.docs: I worked on the backend and integration flow for embeddable lead capture forms. The system supports forms embedded on external websites, validates incoming submissions, checks subscription eligibility, and creates the corresponding records within the correct celebrant account. The workflow also connects submissions to invitations and notifications.

interactions.docs: Visitors can submit enquiries directly from a celebrant's website without navigating to MyCelebrant. Submitted information enters the celebrant's existing lead management workflow, reducing manual data entry and keeping enquiries organized.

complexities.docs: The main engineering challenge was supporting submissions originating from external websites while preserving account boundaries. The workflow also needed to coordinate validation, record creation, subscription checks, and downstream actions reliably.

security.docs: The backend uses tenant-scoped validation to associate submissions with the correct account. Subscription enforcement, rate limiting, and transactional creation help protect the public-facing integration and maintain data consistency.

overview: Backend development for Scrubbe, a security and operations platform featuring incident management, service-level tracking, integrations, and an AI assistant called Ezra that helps users explore operational information.

development.docs: I worked on TypeScript and Node.js backend services using Prisma and PostgreSQL. My contributions included incident-related functionality and the AI assistant Ezra, which interprets natural-language requests into structured parameters such as timeframes, priorities, and search terms.

interactions.docs: Ezra helps users request incident summaries and explore operational information through natural language. The assistant interprets prompts and supports streaming responses, allowing users to receive generated summaries progressively.

complexities.docs: One challenge was converting flexible natural-language requests into predictable parameters that backend services could use. This included extracting relevant timeframes, priorities, and search terms while supporting sensible defaults when users did not specify every detail.

security.docs: The application handles operational incident information through backend services. The implementation used the application's existing data access and authentication architecture rather than exposing unrestricted database access through the AI assistant.

overview: Jottaware is a multi-tenant work management SaaS for freelancers and small teams. It brings organizations, clients, projects, tasks, time tracking, notes, reporting, and real-time communication into one workspace.

development.docs: I built Jottaware with a Go backend using Fiber, PostgreSQL, and GORM, alongside a React and TypeScript frontend. The backend provides APIs for organizations, clients, projects, tasks, time entries, notes, notifications, and workspace management. The platform also includes background jobs, reporting, file handling, and invitation workflows.

interactions.docs: Jottaware supports collaboration through workspace invitations, client-facing workflows, and real-time communication using WebSockets. Users can organize their work, track time, manage project progress, and receive notifications without constantly refreshing the application.

complexities.docs: Building a multi-tenant SaaS required careful attention to data ownership, organization boundaries, and user permissions. Another challenge was coordinating real-time communication, scheduled notifications, and time tracking while maintaining consistent application state.

security.docs: The backend uses JWT-based authentication, refresh-token handling, password hashing, and authorization checks. Organization and resource ownership rules help ensure users only access information belonging to workspaces they are permitted to use.

learning.docs: Building Jottaware has strengthened my understanding of multi-tenant backend architecture, authentication, real-time systems, background processing, and SaaS product development. It has also given me experience making technical decisions across the entire product, from database design to deployment.
